bullets.title: Fed hike near-certain today; Warsh's less-guided approach risks dovish read
bullets.body: Market pricing 90-94% odds of a 25bp Fed hike this afternoon, with consensus expecting minimal forward guidance from Chair Warsh. Multiple desks flag risk the meeting is perceived as a 'dovish hike' if messaging is unclear on policy path; JPM expects only two hikes total this year (Sep/Dec) vs. market pricing 53bp additional through year-end. 10Y yield closed at 5.00% (new cycle high) and bond traders have built extreme short positions ahead of the decision.

bullets.title: S&P futures +0.37% pre-market; oil down ~2% as Saudi supply signals weigh
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures trading +0.37% to 7684.5 as of pre-market Wednesday; 10-year yield at 4.98%, up 2bps. Oct WTI crude down 1.89% to $103.83 on Saudi Arabia supply normalization signals and reports of US-China discussing tariff cuts on energy/agricultural products ahead of the Trump-Xi summit Sept 24. Asian and European markets broadly higher overnight.

bullets.title: $6.9T options expiry on Sept 18 (triple-witching); single-stock OI 20% above YTD average
bullets.body: Citi flags $6.9tn notional open interest expiring Sept 18 — the largest September expiry in recent history — split $5tn indices, $952bn ETFs, $998bn single stocks; this represents 8.8% of Russell 3000 market cap. Single-stock options volumes running 20% above YTD average. Historically triple-witching days show lower intra-day volatility, though 2026 witching days (n=2) have been above historical average.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning: Mag7 at 95th percentile; semis net sold; software seeing short covers
bullets.body: GS Prime reports hedge funds net sold global equities over the past month with the largest US macro selling since 'Liberation Day' and ETF shorts rising at fastest pace in 6 months. TMT is the most net-bought US sector; Mag 7 net allocation risen to ~20% (95th percentile 3-year), while Semis/Semi Equipment is the most net-sold subsector. Software is seeing short covers with long exposure near lows, creating a positioning tailwind.

bullets.title: Retail investor basket down -26% from May peak; VIX broke above 16.55 trend signal
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags the 'High Retail Investor Sentiment' basket is down -26% from its May 28 peak and now -3% YTD, with the cohort down -2.0% just yesterday. VIX closed above the 16.55 Hedgeye TREND signal level after crowd panic-bought SPY puts; short-dated 10-day calendar vol jumped from 12 to 20. SPX immediate-term risk range cited as 7521–7747.

bullets.title: AI safety debate resolves bullish for compute: agentic workloads 100x more demanding than 2023 chat
bullets.body: Multiple desks (Citi, JPM, GS) conclude that AI safety and alignment concerns are compute-intensive, driving MORE demand rather than less — frontier model developers view safety as requiring significant GPU/infrastructure investment. Agentic AI workloads are cited as 100x more demanding than 2023 chat models, with NVIDIA Vera Rubin delivering 30x better AI factory throughput on agentic tasks. AI trade stabilized after initial safety-debate selloff, with semis recovering ~50bps vs. software down ~1.3%.

bullets.title: SK Hynix-Intel US memory deal: exploratory talks confirmed; nothing finalized; INTC +3.3% pre-market
bullets.body: Reuters reported SK Hynix in early talks with Intel to lease part of Intel's Ohio facility or form a JV with cloud firms to produce memory chips in the US for the first time; SK Hynix clarified nothing has been finalized. White House is pressing SK Hynix and Samsung to expand US memory investment and weighing semiconductor tariffs with relief conditional on foreign investment. INTC +3.3% and MU +0.9% pre-market on the reports.

bullets.title: TSMC to hike prices across all nodes in 2027; Q4 DRAM +20% QoQ, NAND +30% QoQ forecast
bullets.body: JPM Chips for Breakfast notes TSMC plans to hike prices across all nodes in 2027 (vs. leading-edge only in 2026), with OSAT pricing spreading to wirebonding. Q4 DRAM contract prices forecast to rise ~20% QoQ and NAND flash ~30% QoQ as AI server demand absorbs capacity. TSMC 3nm, 2nm, and CoWoS capacity severely constrained in Q3 with Nvidia and Apple dominating allocation.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex cycle intact: 13% net debt/equity leverage, Meta expanding Utah campus 4th time
bullets.body: JPM and multiple desks see no imminent capex downturn signal; hyperscaler net debt-to-equity at 13% with accelerating cloud OCF growth and equity/debt issuance capacity supports strong growth over next two years. Meta expanding its Eagle Mountain, Utah data center campus for the fourth time; frontier AI model vendors could generate $20-40bn annual revenue per GW vs. $10bn in 2025.

bullets.title: AI pacing/safety debate favors hyperscalers over semis in near term; Software-Semis spread at ATH
bullets.body: Citi notes the AI pacing debate has pushed capex timing out, benefiting hyperscalers (CGUSHYPR +9% QTD) over semis (CGUSSEMI -28% QTD). The Software-to-Semis pair hit an all-time high one-day move of +12% on Anthropic CEO comments. Hedge funds de-risked crowded US Semis (-0.8 std dev) ahead of FOMC; IGV has returned -3.9% YTD vs. S&P 500 +12.7% YTD.

bullets.title: OpenAI mulling $1.2T valuation funding round ahead of IPO
bullets.body: OpenAI is in early talks for a new funding round at a $1.2 trillion valuation, which would occur before the company goes public, per FT. Anthropic and Salesforce CEOs separately noted businesses are using only 5-10% of AI's full value potential.

bullets.title: 3Q ad growth expected to reaccelerate to ~13% YoY; META and AMZN favored on scaled platform consolidation
bullets.body: UBS expects 3Q digital ad growth to reaccelerate to ~13% YoY driven by political spending, budget flush, and AI-driven monetization improvements. META and AMZN are flagged as beneficiaries of budget consolidation toward scaled platforms. META CEO Zuckerberg framed alignment as a key AI differentiator and launched Meta One subscription service starting at $2.99/month.

bullets.title: FOMC expected 10-2 vote; Waller and Bowman likely dissenters; December hike still possible
bullets.body: UBS and multiple desks model the FOMC vote as 10-2 to hike 25bp, with Governors Waller and Bowman dissenting. Market pricing implies 53bp of additional hikes through year-end; JPM expects only two total this year (Sep/Dec). Key market focus is on dot plot and the policy path's impact on long-end yields, which already sit at a new cycle high of 5.00%.

bullets.title: Retail sales print expected today: +0.8% m/m August vs. July's -0.6% decline
bullets.body: August retail sales consensus is +0.8% m/m with core retail sales expected +0.4% vs. prior -0.4% decline. The bounce would represent a meaningful reversal following July's weakness and is a key data input for the Fed narrative around consumer resilience vs. slowdown risk.

bullets.title: Oil above $100/bbl remains structural headwind; Iran war adds geopolitical risk premium
bullets.body: WTI above $100/bbl is flagged by JPM as a structural equity headwind; mid-$80s would be a bullish catalyst. Iran war has cost the Pentagon $38B+ through August with monthly costs at $2-3B; Saudi Arabia's key oil pipeline remains offline due to attacks with the kingdom pivoting sales to Asia via Hormuz. Trucking linehaul index also surged 11.3% YoY in August, compounding cost pressures across the economy.

bullets.title: UK CPI accelerated to 3.1% in August; BoE expected to hold now, hike in November
bullets.body: UK headline CPI rose to 3.1% YoY in August from 2.9%, driven by energy. Core inflation held at 2.6% and services at 3.4%, but supercore services reaccelerated to 3.6% on 3m/3m annualized basis. JPM forecasts CPI peak of 3.9% in February 2027 (assuming $100 oil declining to $90 by early 2027) with a November BoE hike now the base case.

bullets.title: CLARITY Act fails Senate cloture; near-term headwind for crypto brokers HOOD, CRDO
bullets.body: The CLARITY Act failed to secure 60 Senate votes (missed by 11), sharply reducing near-term enactment odds. Circle (CRDO) fell 11.4% on the vote. Morgan Stanley sees SEC/CFTC rulemaking advancing within existing authority as the alternative path, but the legislative failure is a near-term negative for Coinbase, Robinhood, and Gemini.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi summit Sept 24 a key macro catalyst; tariff cuts on energy/agriculture being discussed
bullets.body: US and China are reported to be weighing tariff cuts on energy and agricultural products ahead of the leaders' summit on September 24. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang is expected to attend the Trump-Xi dinner. The summit is flagged by multiple desks as among the key macro catalysts alongside BoE and BOJ meetings in the coming weeks.

bullets.title: China August data soft: factory output +0.8% m/m, retail sales flat, FAI contracted 10.6% YoY
bullets.body: JPM lowered its 3Q China GDP forecast to 3.6% annualized following mixed August data: factory output +0.8% m/m, retail sales flat, fixed asset investment contracted 10.6% YoY. Online retail sales accelerated modestly to 3.3% YoY in August vs. 2.3% in July, with home appliances returning to positive growth (+2.3% YoY) for the first time since February. HSCEI 3M implied vol sits at just the 10th percentile despite a dense US-China catalyst calendar.

bullets.title: Freight rates surge 11.3% YoY in August; trucking capacity constrained by regulatory and immigration pressures
bullets.body: The Cass Truckload Linehaul Index rose 11.3% YoY in August, accelerating 270bps from July, with shipment volumes inflecting to growth (+2.1% YoY) for the first time since January 2023. Capacity is constrained by English proficiency CDL rules, non-domiciled driver restrictions, ELD enforcement, and federal immigration actions — all adding to diesel cost pressures that particularly pressure low-margin distribution-heavy retailers.
